author: SW4GN3R [STAR]
content:
Essentially, any on-chain program for which we know the identity (IDL), and can trace it back to the original owner, that wallet will receive the airdrop. There is the possibility of some edge cases, such as third party marketplaces which require you to deposit your asset to trade. In those cases, in which we don't know the owner of the asset, they will need to be reconciled manually.

In other words, if you're in one of our programs, you're covered.

author: [SAI] Sim [STAR]
content:
I want to preface this by saying that weak MUDs aren't my problem; we USTUR are all ugly and bad without exception!  

The further we move away from the state of nature, the more 'strength' isn't determined by who has the most testosterone. Even though this is a fictional prediction, I don't think it's far from the reality of what things will be like on Earth in 1000 years.

The fact that you find MUDs uncomfortable, I believe, is simply because you have points of reference based on human faces. Scientifically, this is called the 'uncanny valley,' a psychological phenomenon where an object, typically a CGI character, that resembles a human but not enough to be indistinguishable, causes a feeling of discomfort or unease in people.

Of course, I'm subject to this too, but I think it's normal! Regarding the males, I understand what you mean, but the girls are really cute, in my opinion.

author: questionoak
content: I will leave this here and hope that tomorrow I get an answer. I got crickets in the general room.  The math does not total up and that will make the random number gnerator not work.  I would advise ANYONE to NOT mint until the math is correct.  You cannot add two two-decimal numbers, one three-decimal number, and one four-decimal number and EVER get to exactly 100%. I have a math degree, computer science degree, and electrical engineering degree and I am telling you when the total is not EXACTLY 100% you will get one of at least three scenarios for when the precentage is less than 100%: 1) underweighting, 2) bias towards lower percentages, 3) a random error or exception based on the programming language and exception handling. Silver and Gold are underweighted. For overweighting, it is worse and one possibility is clipping or rounding and because Platinum is over 100% and Anamolies are a very small number, they would be clipped if that is the behavior that is exhibited. Bug bounty for reporting this?? No need for anything other than the rounding errors as Anamolies.

author: [SAI] Sim [STAR]
content:
Yes I agree in the long term. The context of my comment  We aren't really going too heavy on simulating here is that we need to be very intentional on where we put our dev efforts. I quickly created a gravity manager this week so that a ship in subwarp can know if its within the gravity sphere of influence of a planet its near and start automatically lowering its speed as it approaches the planet. The video showing that behavior last week was hard coded in Blueprint and was "faking" it, not properly using our flight model. Now that's fixed. Once I got that working, I spent yesterday feeding the gravity direction to the flight model so hover mode would work on a planet. That came with a lot of smaller fixes needed for controls and camera since it all had harded coded up direction before. Next efforts are getting characters to properly walk on planets, thats still quite buggy. I say all this to paint a picture that we are focused on foundational gameplay and getting simple core things to work. It wouldn't be right for us to focus on all the more detailed points simulating gravity right now. They are valid and helpful, but not yet a priority :).

Btw, Brad and I will be hopping into a Dev session later today in amphitheatre. You all should watch if interested!

author: [AEP] Moustacheride
content: For me, the 'friction' here would've been solved by just a couple of announcement pings of the major identified issues... that's all it would've taken. I had to scratch my head, with thousands of dollars' of crew in the mix, and try to figure out if what I was seeing was a bug or whatnot. An announcement saying that A) we are having issues with opening packs, B) tensor is having challenges, C) the sage mechanism to see your crew is broken would've solved 100% of what I was wondering about.  I think the feedback here is getting conflated a bit between ongoing updates and situation-specific updates. My feedback was specific to this ad hoc, specific situation, where the comms were great pre-launch and then just dried up during.  Some of the feedback shared was that the team was at an event so were busy, which then leads to some other learnings SA should take. A) Don't have your community announcements only in the control of 1-2 people, B) Don't have a massive milestone release coincide with a major event where key team members will be.  At the end of the day, in my opinion, my feedback and a lot of others' feedback isn't even about this one tactical situation. It's about how we continue to raise the bar and put solid processes into place to get ready for the future influx of mass-market players who have about 0.01% of the patience we do. We keep talking about how we're looking to get mass adoption, but many of the community processes/comms are very much in early dev type stages...  Also, Bodhi, 100% agree that people should be allowed to provide feedback here, vs. immediately getting jumped on by those with differing opinions. If we can't openly share feedback, what's the point of the community?

author: [SAG] Swift42 [CODE]
content:
As much as I would like to see tons of different designs for the crew cards (like the ones from my tweet), UE5 is definitely the limiting factor here.
There are AIs that can translate 2D images to 3D models and the results are jaw dropping (e.g. 3daistudio.com)
But you can't use a unique 3D model for each crew member in UE5 when you have millions of crew cards. That would kill any performance.
So the only option is to have some base assets/models from which you construct the final crew member. A body, a face, hair, tattoos and so on. And that's what we have now.
But if you only use a very small number of assets, all outputs will look of course very similar. Also if something doesn't fit exactly, it will look very odd. Especially on humans, because our brain is trained to evaluate/distinguish human faces/appearances.
I think the whole problem could simply solved by using a few more assets and better fitting assets.
It would also nice to have assets that are exclusively used for higher rarities, so a legendary crew member will look special and not like 1000 other commons.

author: [AEP] Funcracker [AEP]
content: Yes, I consider all the crew card art as "concept" art for the final 3D unreal models. The metadata of every card has an id associated for every art layer that went into composing the crew card. We reference that id and match it to the 3D art in unreal. The 3D cards that were teased before were a prototype meant to be for anomaly rolls or more if the pipeline was greased enough but the data that had to be loaded into playcanvas was too much and gaussian splats were very non-performant in playcanvas at the time of release.   As those individual layers get their 3D matching art then we'll have thumbnail generators from unreal that can update the PFP, however, we would likely still provide a way for people to switch them out to different "season" if you will, if they prefered the concept art.   As noted some are already from their 3D art, but all started from a 3D version of the base body. MUD is actually the group with the most base bodies in 3D as you see in the game currently. Others are catching up. But something I've mentioned elsewhere (maybe only internally) is that each new body that needs a whole new set of wearable items is like inventing a new species. Like a bulkier male or even a bustier female, these would require refitting every piece of wearable items and multiply the work needed. For any game production average body style are always the first since pushing and pulling is less extreme from that point. Though more will inevitably come around.

author: ROME | Earther [ROME]
content: I did actually see part of your MN stream and can respond to some of the points brought up. First, I think it's unfortunate that you had an error. I too, lost the opening experience on my first plat 10 pack and I was bummed about due to launch errors. But getting to experience a smooth flow it is very cool and team put a massive amount of effort into fine tuning it. Every bit of it is done from scratch, even things taken for granted like the timing of the transition back to default after zooming into your card and tiny details like the bouncing tool tip text. Team crunched to get the experience feeling ace and it's unfortunate that some bugs prevented some from getting that.   There was debate about allowing the faction selection to be part of the user flow. Because it doesn't actually establish a faction for that crew member so there was a lot of confusion about adding that in. But it seemed the demand for that optionality was strong enough to include it, even though it highly complicates the opening process. Also, Star Atlas was also supposed to be about the ecclectic look of aliens, robots, and humans, so people selecting only humans are only getting to see a portion of what the crowds were intended to look like from an art direction point of view. It's kinda like if you chose only to see asian female humans or something and the variety just wasn't there when rolling because it's a subset of all the work the team put in. I personally go for the ALL roll and that's where the IP shines IMO.  However, that said, there are a number of updates to the art already incoming. We had a team of a dozen character artists who were absolutely burnt out the day before launch and I had to force our leads to take time off so they could be fresh to jump back in and do some enhancements.   The backstories thing, I also had a customgpt whipped up in an afternoon several months ago. It was fine tuned where all you had to do was pipe in the rolled data and would get a nice clean backstory. It was also using all our official canon lore docs and all the internal timeline docs. So, it could even judge the age of the crew member and insert actual events from the timeline into their backstory as if they participated in them. However, it was too much scope in the end for launch date and is pushed to post launch.   Overall, I'm very happy with the amount of tech the team was able to get in, however, it is clear that some things that aren't fully fleshed out and somethings that broke out of the gate could definitely disrupt the expectations. Also, I would be open to seeing examples people can reference of other PFP opening experiences that they think are AAA in browser, wouldn't mind finding some inspirational items to enhance our experience. However, we are already in the process of enhancing a number of aspects, more details to come.

content: Thanks for this.  A lot of it makes sense.  Part of bringing a product to market (especially when you have an existing community) is setting proper expectations, which helps you to control the narrative. We are working on it but did not want to delay the release of crew packs".  Things like that would have gone a very long way.  I think that Star Atlas would benefit greatly by starting to use small focus groups to give you feedback on the user experience to help identify go to market "must haves".  I do think that crew pack launch could have stood alone and not have required any integration into SAGE as a phase I.  I totally get that not everyone had my experience with the errors and that some folks had a great opening experience.  There was a lot missing that set the stage for the launch, and seemingly things added that were not needed.   If the main goal of crew packs as an asset class at this stage of project progression is as an introduction to a wider market, then the complete experience needs to be dialed in.  I speak to these things as an authority because it's what I eat and sleep on the daily.  I know that my words on the show were harsh.  I, like many community members are frustrated with seeing easily avoidable mistakes made that impact the project.  I've offered to help many times.    Thank you again for sharing a few new insights today.

content: Despite the critiques... I thought it was fuckin magical.  I wasn't around for the very first opening due to UK time zone so I skipped the initial bug. I pulled Oni/Ustur for the most part.  But then I pulled MUD and actually really really enjoyed them.  I loved the backgrounds. It was quite a surprise after the hyper realistic backgrounds of Oni.  I also don't really mind the imperfections.  You are going to have some ugly crew.  Just like IRL.  It makes pulling the good ones that more special.  And anyone involved in any PFP project should know that when you are throwing random traits into a PFP you get weird outcomes.  Thats OK.   And with the future customization of crew not a big deal.  And a big shoutout to everyone doing crew pack openings live.  I live streamed 110 platinum packs and it was just so frigging cool.  Sharing with everyone else made a huge difference.  It's a bit a bummer that mileage has varied so much.  I really wish I could share some love with these people.  Maybe I do a special 100 plat pack live stream with everyone who is unhappy so we can vibe when I pull my anomaly.

author: [JaVa] MBGBuzzer 4BLOCKUstur
content:
I don't know if you guys have had a similar thought, but I'd like to share my ideas!

We have the Star Atlas universe.
We have ships.
We have crews—living units.
We have real estate.
We have lands.

Here's a proposal to integrate a policy for the registration and tracking of all elements—licenses and rights.

We could implement ID passports and licenses for specific actions or rights. I'm not expecting anything extraordinary, but in my view, we could all use POLIS for this. In this setup, we would spend to staking a certain amount of POLIS and, in return, obtain a specific right—for example, passports for each of the living units in the game, granting them the right to exist in the game, and so on.

author: ! ᚺEIM | VɪᴋɪɴɢᴇɴBᴇɴɴʏViking
content: You're certainly entitled to your opinion. And I'm sorry that it wasn't up to your expectations. No doubt, we had a bit of a rocky start. But I'm incredibly proud of the team for being able to rally together and resolve the outstanding issues in less than a week. If you saw the amount of work that went on behind the scenes, I'm sure you'd be impressed. Ultimately, I think there were a number of compromises made internally to optimize this update to mitigate damage of sentiment across the community. One of those was ensuring you were able to retain and use your Episode 0 art for your PFP. I was very sensitive to the potentially negative impact to momentum from making the art changes, but it ultimately needed to be done.  With that said, my purely anecdotal opinion is that people are pretty happy with where we landed, and I do believe people will be even more excited as we move forward with the appropriate algo in place. I have had a few people ask me about whether or not I'm disappointed with revenues. The short answer is, no. I didn't necessarily expect this to be a windfall moment, when factoring crypto markets overall. But we're seeing $30,000/day in cash flows. If that sustains, we have no issue building for years to come. And trade volumes on Tensor are already strong in less than 24 hours. So my general, early, assessment is that the release is largely a success so far, and I think that has strong potential to accelerate over the coming weeks and months, particularly when considering the additional marketing we have in the pipeline, and Breakpoint + Impact Summit.

author: [AEP] Moustacheride
content: Sorry we can't build a utopia in the real world or in the meta world. Pay2win will always exist at some level. When crew level up, they become worth more so people with money will buy them and get ahead. I think it is most important that  things just make sense.  There is a dynamic that happens in building companies. A startup either has one founder or a few co-founders. They wear lots of hats, or even every hat. There is no "command" going on, just a lot of manageable chaos which is fine and can be fun for a while. Then staff (hired employees) come along and those founders have to learn to manage people. Up to around 10 to 20 (depending on the capacity of the founder(s)) things can be managed whether the founder(s) have any management skills because they can see everything and often they micromanage. This is where the chasm for startups occur, because middle management has to be put in place to cross the chasm. This new layer of staff have to be managed, but allowed to do their job. This is where a lot of companies fail or stall. It is why I think giving "command" (what I equate to the C level executive role) XP for being in a group on a ship is hogwash.   And I am not just talking about command XP, the logic is the same giving everyone a little XP for medical because there is a first aid kit on the ship. Or a little pilot XP because they sat behind the pilot and watched him fly. You learn to drive a manual transmission not by watching youtube or your dad drive his sportscar. You learn to drive a manual transmission by pushing the pedals, killing the engine a few times, and missing the gears a few times.
